claims.text: A machine-learning-driven optimization strategy integrating CALPHAD thermodynamic modeling and DFT-based descriptors can rapidly screen and design intrinsically strong, ductile, low-weight RHEA compositions.
The initial refractory multi-principal-element composition space contains varied phase equilibria and microstructures.
Machine-learning-guided high-throughput screening can use CALPHAD and DFT calculations to select optimal RHEA compositions.
High-temperature synthesis and controlled cooling are processing conditions typical of refractory-alloy development.
CALPHAD modeling can predict phase stability and microstructural evolution in the proposed RHEA space.
Predicted phase stability and microstructural evolution control the formation of strengthening phases and ductile matrices.
Integrating machine learning with thermodynamic and electronic-structure simulations identifies compositional descriptors correlated with enhanced mechanical properties.
The identified descriptors enable rapid selection of compositions with favorable intrinsic mechanical properties.
The strategy will identify novel RHEA compositions that can be experimentally validated.
The selected RHEAs will have superior strength and ductility relative to RHEAs designed through traditional thermo-kinetic methods.
The selected RHEAs will have lower density than RHEAs designed through traditional thermo-kinetic methods.
The method is expected to be effective mainly when the refractory element set and processing conditions resemble those represented in model training.
Performance may differ in alloy systems having substantially different elemental interactions.
